shared_elements: zoomorphic/serpentine creature with a head at one end
low-relief carving on a stone panel
justification: Both surfaces carry incised low-relief imagery that includes a long curving zoomorphic form terminating in an animal-like head with an open snout, and A's border of scrolls and serpentine elements is loosely comparable in linear convention to B's single sinuous creature. But A is a densely populated narrative scene with multiple seated and standing human figures, elaborate headdresses, a central tree/cross motif and framing bands, whereas B shows only one sparse, isolated, highly schematic curving creature on an otherwise blank field.
